_README: Template for a Mechanical or Aero Balance sweep. Copy to
balance-<car>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.json, fill in `car`/`build`, then fill the `mb`
(or `ab`) field on each row as you read it. Rows may be filled in any
order and partially — the solver ignores rows with a null readout, so you
can run it after five readings to see whether the sweep is discriminating
yet.
node tests/fit-balance.js tests/data/balance-<car>-<date>.json
MECHANICAL BALANCE IS ALREADY SOLVED ON THE GR86 (2026-08-12):
MB = R / (F + R)
F  = arF + 0.150 x spF + 50.5
R  = arR + 0.150 x spR + 72.3
It is the REAR axle's share of roll stiffness. So this template is no
longer for discovering the model — it is for testing whether the STRUCTURE
holds on another car. It should, because it is roll stiffness. The three
coefficients should not, because they are that car's tires, geometry and
weight distribution.
SO THE JOB CHANGED. Rows 1-3 are now the whole thing on a new car: equal
bars, then the same-ratio pair. If MB is still the rear share and the pair
still splits, the form holds and only the numbers move. Rows 4-7 refine the
coefficients; the long bar sweeps that used to be rows 8-15 are RETIRED,
because re-sweeping one bar against a solved linear model measures nothing.
ONE VARIABLE PER ROW. Every row states what it holds. If something else
moved, the row is discarded, not interpreted.
HOLD AND RECORD TIRE PRESSURE. It moves MB — measured, 31.5 to 50 psi
shifted the readout a step with bars, springs and ride height untouched.
It lives inside the axle constants. A sweep that lets it drift will blame
the bars for a tire effect.
NOTHING MAY SAY 'SIMULATING...' WHEN A ROW IS RECORDED. The panel is still
recomputing and the number is stale. This cost two rows the first day the
rule existed, one of them half the same-ratio pair.
Record MB/AB to every digit the game prints. And note what two decimals
can and cannot do: anything in [0.445, 0.455] prints as 0.45, so a single
row agreeing with a model to four decimals is a coincidence, not a
confirmation. Two conclusions died that way on the day this was measured.

baseline.note: the app's own values for this car, used as the hold-point for the bar sweeps
baseline.pressureNote: TIRE PRESSURE IS IN HERE BECAUSE IT MOVES MB. Measured 2026-08-12: 31.5 -> 50.0 psi shifted Mechanical Balance 0.51 -> 0.50 with bars, springs and ride height all untouched. No candidate model M1-M5 has a tire term, and tire stiffness sits in series with the spring and the bar in the roll-stiffness chain. Hold it and record it on every row, or the sweep will blame the bars for a tire effect.

rows.purpose: DIRECTION AND OFFSET — equal bars. On the GR86 this read 0.51, NOT 0.50, and the axle constants are why. If a new car also reads off 0.5 with equal bars, the constants are real there too
SAME-RATIO PAIR (a) — with row 3, separates a pure ratio from anything with an additive term

SAME-RATIO PAIR (b) — identical 1:2 as row 2 at near-double magnitude. Equal readouts = pure ratio; different = additive terms. On the GR86: 0.54 vs 0.56, so the terms are real. NOTE 40/80 was the original plan and is UNREACHABLE — the bar slider maxes at 65
SPRINGS (a) — bars held at 30/30, front spring -30%. Expect MB to RISE: a softer front means the rear's share grows
SPRINGS (b) — bars held at 30/30, front spring +30%. Expect MB to FALL. Rows 4-5 also give this car's bar-to-spring exchange rate, which was 1 bar point to 6.7 lb/in on the GR86

RIDE HEIGHT (a) — bars 30/30, springs back at baseline, front ride height at MINIMUM. Untested on any car, and now a PREDICTION rather than an exploration: ride height sits inside the axle constants on the GR86 evidence, so the solved model says it should move MB and roughly by how much

RIDE HEIGHT (b) — front ride height at MAXIMUM. If rows 6-7 move MB, the axle constants are partly geometric and the model needs a ride-height term; if they do not, the constants are tires and mass alone

TIRE PRESSURE — bars 30/30, everything else at baseline, pressure moved a long way at BOTH ends. Measured on the GR86: 31.5 to 50 psi shifted MB a step. Equal movement at both ends still shifting the balance means the axles do not contribute symmetrically, which is worth confirming on a second car

_RETIRED_ROWS: The old rows 8-15 swept arF from 1 to 65 at arR=30 and then the mirror.
They are retired, not merely deprioritised: the model is linear in each
bar, four settings plus the same-ratio pair already determined the form,
and sweeping one bar against a solved linear model measures nothing except
how patient the person holding the controller is.
Bring them back only if row 1 or row 3 on a new car disagrees with the
solved form — at which point the shape is genuinely unknown again and the
sweeps are how you recover it.
_AERO_ROWS: AERO BALANCE HAS A MODEL TOO (2026-08-12), validated out-of-sample:
AB = (F + a) / (F + a + R + b)      a ~ 175 lb, b ~ 215 lb on the GR86
aeF/aeR are POUNDS OF DOWNFORCE, not a percentage — which is why the app's
'% of range' output cannot target the readout at all: a percentage of two
different pound ranges does not determine their ratio. The body makes
downforce comparable to the wings, exactly as case A1 predicted and as a
one-point 'solve' published the same morning wrongly denied.
So rows 4-5 below are no longer only a reachability bracket — they PIN a
and b, which badly need pinning: the two-decimal readout leaves a loose
anywhere between about 85 and 360 lb. And a/b are the bodyshell, so they
are per-car by definition; a second car is owed, not optional.
For an Aero Balance sweep set readout to 'ab', use aeF/aeR instead of
arF/arR, and swap the row plan for:
1  50/50   SYMMETRY — is AB 0.5 with equal sliders? Almost certainly not,
because the body makes downforce the wings do not, and that
asymmetry is the interesting part.
2  25/50   SAME-RATIO PAIR (a)
3  50/100  SAME-RATIO PAIR (b)
4  0/0     FLOOR — both wings at minimum. AB here is the bodyshell's own
balance, and it is the number that decides whether the app's
0.42-0.48 target is reachable on this car at all.
5  100/100 CEILING — both at maximum. With row 4 this brackets every AB
the car can produce; if the target band sits outside that
bracket, the app is printing an unreachable goal.
6-9        aeF sweep at aeR=50: 0, 25, 75, 100
10-11      rake: ride height F min then max, wings held at 50/50 — tests
whether AB is a pure wing function or moves with attitude
12         one row on a second car at 0/0, to see whether the floor is a
property of the car rather than a constant
